category_title: Medium-proficiency students who struggle with run-on sentences and L1/L2 translation issues
minimal_context: The student is working individually in the classroom to revise the second draft of their Personal Narrative assignment.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Please take out the second draft of your Personal Narrative assignment so we can work on revising it.

STUDENT: I looked at it, but after the revision of my second draft, I found more errors and they were the same. Like before, those were mostly the run-on and repeated sentences.

TUTOR: Okay, let's just try to correct those sentences now.

STUDENT: It is difficult for me to correct my essay. I understand how hard to organize thoughts and choose the correct words. I'm from Korea, and there they don't teach how to organize thoughts and write an essay.

TUTOR: Just do your best to write what you mean.

STUDENT: Because of the problems with use of English language, I lost confidence in writing. I found it hard because there were errors in almost all my essay. Since I am not a good talker, I had troubles with expressing my thoughts in a proper way.

options.A: Use desk carrels during essay revision to provide personal space and distinguish individual from group areas.
options.B: Engage in shared discourse and provide direct instruction in coping strategies during the revision routine.
options.C: Provide noncontingent attention throughout the writing session and ignore problem behaviors that function to gain attention.
options.D: Require three revisions per narrative assignment and only grade the final, third essay draft.
